Metadata.title: easyrender: the 3D engine to sell, design and play
Metadata.description: Turn one product photo into a 3D model with real scale, materials and physics. Use it in your store with AR, in architectural renders and in game engines, or let your AI agent do it over MCP.

Footer.tagline: Your agent turns product and listing photos into 3D models you can spin, embed and open in AR.
Footer.pricesNote: Prices in USD. Credits never expire.

connect.title: Or let your agent do it
connect.description: easyrender speaks MCP, so any agent that supports it can create renders, check them and build 3D models on your credits.

connect.a: easyrender is an MCP server. Add it to Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client with your API key, and your agent can turn photos into 3D models on its own. Everything it makes shows up in your web dashboard.

needAgent.q: Do I need an agent to use it?
needAgent.a: No. You can upload photos in the web app, one by one or in bulk from your library. The agent just lets you run it on autopilot.

photos.a: One sharp, well lit photo where the whole object is visible, ideally on a plain background. Catalogue shots and listing photos of a single piece or a building front work great.

scope.a: Furniture, decor objects and building exteriors. Whole interior rooms are not supported yet. Fine logos and small text come out soft.

output.a: A textured GLB for the web and a USDZ for iPhone Quick Look, plus a hosted 3D viewer you can share or embed on a listing.

freePreview.a: Before building the model we draw the object from every angle. You check that preview for free and only spend credits when it looks right.

failed.a: Failed renders are refunded to your balance automatically.

public.a: Finished models appear in the public gallery by default. You can hide any of yours from its page at any time.

AgentDemo.ask: Here is the spring catalogue. Make a 3D model of every product and add them to the listings.
AgentDemo.done: Done. 24 models are in your easyrender library, with GLB and USDZ for AR. Here is the first one:

claudeAi.one: Open claude.ai → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
claudeAi.two: Paste this URL as the connector URL.

claudeAi.note: The same sign-in works for any MCP client that supports OAuth. Each connection creates a key you can revoke below.

hero.title: The 3D engine to sell, design and play
hero.stackLabel: One object seen through five passes of the engine. Drag to turn it.

pipeline.lead: Upload one photo. The engine does the rest.
pipeline.body: It rebuilds your product's geometry, materials and real scale, and shows you every angle before you pay.
pipeline.noteBody: The engine draws the object from every side before it builds the mesh. If something is off, you see it before you spend a credit.

industries.body: The same piece is tried in a shopper's living room, dropped into a studio's render and falls with its real weight inside a game.

store.title: One button on your product page
store.body: “View in your space” opens the shopper's camera and places the product at real scale. No app, on iPhone and Android.
store.link: Talk to us about AR for stores

interior.title: Real pieces for your renders
interior.body: Architects, interior designers and lighting designers bring in furniture and fixtures that exist and that the client can buy.

games.title: Props with physics built in

games.link: Connect it over the API or MCP

tools.lead: It looks real. It behaves real.
tools.body: Every element ships with what an engine needs to use it, not only with how it looks.

wheel.lead: It enters the hub once. It works everywhere.
wheel.body: The store uploads its catalogue, the studio uses it in its projects and the client ends up buying the piece they saw in the render.
